paper_title: Associations between magnesium depletion score and depression among individuals aged 20 to 60 years
study_design: Secondary pooled cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2005–2018
claim: The pooled NHANES 2005–2018 cross-sectional analysis included 18,247 adults aged 20–60 years; 1,753 met the study's PHQ-9 threshold of at least 10.
context: These are unweighted participant counts after the stated exclusions. PHQ-9 reflects self-reported symptoms in the preceding two weeks; the threshold classification is not an independently confirmed clinical diagnosis or incident depression outcome.
source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 2, Methods 2.1–2.2 and Fig. 1; pp. 3–4, Table 1.
scope_does_not_establish: ["That magnesium depletion causes depression, or that lowering MDS or magnesium supplementation prevents or treats depression.","A validated clinical diagnosis, depression screening rule, individual prognosis or treatment threshold derived from MDS.","Direct measurement of serum or whole-body magnesium, or proof that magnesium mediates the observed medication associations.","Proof of linearity from P=0.084, identical effects across subgroups, or statistical significance in every subgroup.","Numerical results from Supplementary Tables 1–2, which were referenced by the paper but not obtained for this audit."]
limitations: ["The cross-sectional design cannot establish temporal direction; reverse causation and residual confounding remain possible (Discussion, p. 5).","MDS combines medication use, kidney function and drinking behavior; it is not a biochemical magnesium measurement, and serum-magnesium comparison was unavailable (Methods 2.3; Discussion, p. 5).","PHQ-9 at least 10 is the study's questionnaire-based outcome, not an independently adjudicated clinical diagnosis (Methods 2.2).","Participants with specified missing data were excluded.
